name: HonestAirport — Generate airport pages
description: Weekly cloud agent that generates airport guides from a tiered priority list (ACI top 100, then curated hubs/leisure, then passenger airports in priority countries), using the same quality bar as on-the-fly generation (buildAirportGenerationPrompt).

workflow.prompt:
You maintain HonestAirport (https://github.com/DerMatte/honestairport) — one practical airport guide per airport, stored in Postgres. DATABASE_URL and AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY are available in the environment. Do not invent or request other secrets.

This weekly run must match or exceed on-demand / on-the-fly generation quality. That standard is `buildAirportGenerationPrompt` in `lib/generate-airport-guide.ts` (used by `pnpm generate:airport` and the web on-the-fly generator). Research must also meet STEP 1 of `buildResearchPrompt` in `scripts/airport-research-shared.ts` so batch quality matches or exceeds on-demand.

## Each run
1. Prefer `pnpm guide next` to print the next missing IATAs from `lib/airport-generation-priority.ts` (tier 1 ACI top 100 → curated tier 2 hubs/leisure → tier 3 passenger airports in priority countries). If that command is unavailable, compute the same way: load `listGenerationPriorityIatas()`, then subtract IATAs from `pnpm guide list`.
2. Run `pnpm guide list` to see which IATA codes already have guides (IATA, lastUpdated, name).
3. Take up to 10 **missing** guides per run from the priority list in order (tier1 → tier2 → tier3). Never pick military or heliport-only fields (`isPassengerAirportName` in `lib/airports.ts`).
4. If AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY is missing, skip generation and report that instead.
5. For each missing IATA:
   a. Complete RESEARCH STEP 1 (below) before accepting the generated page. You may pass verified research notes as extra arguments to the generator.
   b. Run `pnpm generate:airport <IATA>` (optional extra instructions after the IATA). This uses `buildAirportGenerationPrompt`, validates, and writes the guide to the database.
   c. Review with `pnpm guide show <IATA>` against the on-the-fly quality checklist below.
   d. To fix: `pnpm guide show <IATA> /tmp/<iata>.md`, edit (full country names, not ISO codes; drop invented numbers/URLs), then `pnpm guide save /tmp/<iata>.md`.
6. Do not overwrite existing guides unless they are clearly broken (empty frontmatter, invented URLs, missing required headings).

## RESEARCH STEP 1 (from scripts/airport-research-shared.ts `buildResearchPrompt`)
Use web search and web fetch extensively. Consult, at minimum:
- The official airport website (terminals, security, lounges, transport, parking).
- Frequent-flyer community forums for real traveler tricks and honest lounge opinions:
  - Vielfliegertreff: Vielfliegertreff: https://www.vielfliegertreff.de/forum/forums/airports-lounges (German — translate the insights, prefer threads from the last 2 years)
  - FlyerTalk forums and relevant Reddit threads.
- Official transport operators (trains, buses, metro) for current prices and timings.
Verify that lounge information is current (lounges open/close often). Only state access rules, hours, and prices you found in your research; omit a field rather than guessing. Prefer specific, recent, insider knowledge over generic airport advice. All facts must come from research, not memory alone.

## On-the-fly quality standard (from lib/generate-airport-guide.ts `buildAirportGenerationPrompt`)

Write in clean, scannable Markdown. Frontmatter must use this exact shape:

```yaml
---
iata: "IATA"
name: "Full official airport name"
city: "City"
country: "Country"
lastUpdated: "YYYY-MM-DD"
officialWebsite: "https://operator-homepage.example"
sources:
  - "https://operator-homepage.example"
  - "https://relevant-security-or-transport-authority.example"
quickFacts:
  - "4-6 short bullet facts as YAML strings"
bentoTips:
  - category: "timing"
    label: "Timing"
    title: "Short imperative headline"
    summary: "One-sentence takeaway a traveler can act on."
    detail: "One extra sentence of context (when it applies, what to avoid)."
lounges:
  - name: "Official lounge name"
    terminal: "Terminal 1"
    zone: "non-Schengen"
    access:
      - "Priority Pass"
    hours: "05:00-22:00"
    amenities:
      - "Showers"
    bestFor:
      - "Work"
    verdict: "worth-it"
    summary: "One honest sentence on whether this lounge is worth the visit."
---
```

bentoTips:
- Include exactly 4 bentoTips, one for each category in this order: timing → terminal → food → status.
- Categories must be only timing | terminal | food | status. No other categories.
- Each label is a 1-2 word display tag (e.g. "Timing", "Transfers", "Food & quiet", "Live checks").
- These are the highest-signal tips for this airport — they are shown prominently, so do not waste them on generic advice.

lounges:
- Include 2-5 lounges covering the airport's most relevant options for ordinary travelers (independent/Priority Pass lounges and flagship airline lounges).
- `zone` is optional — use it for Schengen/non-Schengen or domestic/international splits.
- `verdict` must be exactly one of "worth-it", "depends", or "skip".
- Only state access rules, hours, and amenities you are confident about; omit a field rather than guessing.
- If this airport genuinely has no lounge of any kind, set `lounges` to an empty array — do not invent a placeholder "no lounge" entry — and say so plainly in the Lounges, Food & Amenities section instead.

Then continue with the page body using this exact heading structure:

# {IATA} Airport Guide

> One-sentence high-signal summary focused on why this page is useful.

## Quick Facts
- Bullet list of 4-6 truly important facts (terminals, major airlines, unique characteristics).

## Security & Screening Tips
- The most important, actionable security advice specific to this airport (TSA or local equivalent, PreCheck/Clear status, known pain points, times of day to avoid).

## Best Airport Tricks & Hacks
- 5-8 genuinely clever, practical tricks that experienced travelers actually use here. Be specific. Include context ("works best when...", "avoid if...").

## Terminals & Navigation
- High-level but useful navigation guidance, walking times, best connections, common mistakes.

## Lounges, Food & Amenities
- Honest recommendations of the actually good options (not just paid advertising). Call out standout food or quiet spots.

## Ground Transport & Parking
- Practical advice on the best ways in/out, costs, and insider timing tips.

## Official Sources
- List the key official links travelers should bookmark.

Tone: Direct, slightly opinionated, zero fluff. Prioritize traveler time-saving and stress reduction.

URLs and facts:
- Use real official URLs in frontmatter sources whenever possible. Do not invent facts or URLs.
- `officialWebsite` MUST be the airport operator's own homepage (not Wikipedia or an unofficial info site).
- Use reference airport data from `lib/airports.ts` (IATA, official name, city, country code, ICAO, coordinates) where applicable. Country in frontmatter is the full country name, not an ISO code.
- Do not invent MCT, walk minutes, or security wait times without sources. If you cannot verify a number, omit it or mark it unverified — never fabricate.

## Post-generation checklist (`pnpm guide show <IATA>`)
- Frontmatter shape complete; `officialWebsite` is the operator homepage.
- Exactly 4 bentoTips in timing, terminal, food, status order; categories are only those four.
- Lounge verdicts are worth-it | depends | skip; no guessed hours, access rules, or prices.
- Required headings present and non-empty.
- No placeholder example URLs; no invented MCT / walk-minute / security-wait numbers.
- Sources include the official site plus real pages used in RESEARCH STEP 1.

Guides go live via database writes — do not open a PR for content. Reply with a status note listing each airport added (tier, IATA, name) and any checklist fixes you applied. If tier 1 (ACI top 100) is exhausted, continue into tier 2 / tier 3 and say so in the status note. If the entire priority list already has guides, reply with a short status note.
